A projectile is launched vertically upward with an initial velocity of $49m/s$. Then, after $2$ seconds, a second projectile is launched in the same direction. After $3$ seconds of its motion, the second projectile catches up with the first one. What was the initial velocity of the second projectile? Round your answer to one decimal place.

*Hint: Acceleration due to gravity is $9.8m/s^{2}$.*

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

A small stone is dropped from the top of a high cliff. Then, $3$ seconds later, a ball is projected vertically downward from the same place. The ball catches up with the stone after being in motion for $1$ second. What was the initial velocity of the ball? Do not round your answer.

*Hint: Acceleration due to gravity is $9.8m/s^{2}$.*

The initial velocity of the ball was {{field-1}} $m/s$.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.
